objects.alt: A forest road at night with green and violet lanterns floating above it
Bats circle the full moon (animated)

objects.text: The Lantern Road
Night. The fog is thick. Far ahead, lanterns float above the road. What do you do?

objects.alt: A faint ghost in the fog

objects.text: A voice

Halfway down the road, a voice speaks from the fog, close to your ear:

“Don't follow them in the dark. Carry a light of your own, or they will keep you.”

Then it is gone.

objects.alt: A forest road at night with green and violet lanterns floating above it
A bat flying over the forest

objects.text: The Lights
The lanterns lead to an iron gate. Behind it, someone is humming. One lantern drifts close to you.
You catch it. The lantern is warm in your hand.

objects.alt: The lantern you caught, glowing
Your house at the end of the road, every window glowing, the gate open

objects.text: Your House
Your house. Every window glows, but you live alone. The front door is open.

objects.alt: Your room, but older: a bookshelf, a desk with a candle, a moonlit window
A candle you did not light flickers on the desk (animated)

objects.text: Your Room
Your room, but older. A candle you did not light burns on the desk, next to a letter with your name on it.

objects.alt: An old letter sealed with red wax

objects.text: A letter

The ink is brown with age. It is dated 1910.

“Thank you for leaving the door open for me. I will come home soon. I only have to find the way.

— E.”

objects.alt: A moonlit graveyard with crooked tombstones, a bare tree and a small purple ghost
A small ghost girl in a grey dress, turning to look at you

objects.text: The Gate
A girl in a grey dress turns around. “You are the first to stay,” she says.

objects.alt: Eleanor, a small ghost girl with a red ribbon

objects.text: Eleanor

“My name is Eleanor. I live in the big house at the end of the road.

At least, I did. I have been out here a long time.”

objects.alt: Eleanor, looking down at her feet

objects.text: What happened

“I came home late, and Papa locked the door. I followed the lanterns to find another way in.

They never let me go. Without a light, the road just goes round and round.

Will you take me home?”

objects.alt: The road swallowed by fog, only a few lights left
Your lantern, pushing back the fog
Eleanor holding your sleeve

objects.text: Through the fog
Your lantern pushes the fog back, step by step. Eleanor holds your sleeve. The other lights hiss and fall behind.

objects.alt: The old Ashby house at the end of the road, one window lit
Bats circle the full moon (animated)
A lamp glowing in the doorway

objects.text: The Ashby House
The road ends at a tall dark house. A man with a lamp waits at the door. “Eleanor?” he whispers.

objects.alt: The dark hall of your house, a portrait with red eyes on the wall

objects.text: Not alone
You lock the door behind you. Upstairs, someone is humming your favourite song. The end.

objects.alt: A moonlit graveyard with crooked tombstones, a bare tree and a small purple ghost

objects.text: Lost in the fog
You run until the road disappears. The lanterns circle you, patient and silent. The end.

objects.alt: A moonlit graveyard with crooked tombstones, a bare tree and a small purple ghost
Eleanor, smiling, holding your hand

objects.text: A new friend
Her hand is cold, but she smiles. From then on, the lanterns light your way. The end.

objects.alt: The Ashby house at dawn, its door open and lit, gold lights drifting inside

objects.text: Home at last
Father and daughter walk in together. At sunrise the house is empty and quiet. You set them free. The end.

objects.alt: Nothing but fog and a few cold lights on the road

objects.text: Lost together
Without a light, the fog closes in. You and Eleanor walk on forever, two more lanterns on the road. The end.
